#4434. Zonveer ZX3 review: one of the best-value electric dirt bikes for beginners

The Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.

For that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.

Zonveer is a young brand. It launched in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store.

Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page:

A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.

Zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:

With 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.

My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.

And while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.

Range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.

Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the company gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.

The sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy.

We’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.

It’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

#4433. Battlefield 6 streamlines some of the most annoying Challenges yet again, takes out a few of them entirely

The easier and more accessible Battlefield Studios makes those Battlefield 6 Challenges, the better.

The work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done. Having just released a new patch - which already included several updates to Challenges and Assignments - Battlefield Studios has gone in and made even more changes.

This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.

The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge. Now, any headshot beyond 75m will count. Recon Expert 3 is another headshot-themed one that’s been updated, and now requires getting headshot kills beyond 125m, rather than the practically impossible beyond 200m that it required previously.

The Rapid Fire 2 Challenge, which required getting kills beyond 50m with Assault Rifles, has been changed so it now tracks anything beyond 40m. The painful ‘Inflict damage under 15m while hip-firing with Assault Rifles’ has been entirely replaced with one that requires - the far more sensible - inflicting damage while in ADS with Assault Rifles.

A couple of Challenges, such as the one that required suppressing enemies with LMGs, and another that wanted you to deal damage to laser-designated vehicles using lock-on weapons, have both been removed.

The journey to make Challenges and Assignments easier to complete has been a long one. Progression has been one of the key areas of criticism Battlefield 6 received at launch. The issue encompassed more than just slow player and weapon XP earn rates, it also prevented players from accessing new Training Paths for the various classes, and several of the game's weapons.

Battlefield Studios attacked the problem from multiple angles, initially boosting the XP players and their weapons would earn, before later reducing the requirements of the Challenges themselves. The developer continued to streamline those requirements over multiple patches, including majorly overhauling the system earlier this month.

It seems the studio is more confident than ever in the game, as it recently announced that Battlefield 6 will be getting its first free trial next week, offering players who do not own the full game access to iconic modes like Conquest, and Breakthrough - though on an unusual selection of maps.

#4432. Tesla kills $41,990 Model Y AWD: all-wheel drive now costs $8,000 more

Tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator. The cheapest dual-motor Model Y you can order now is the Model Y Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump.

The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla launched it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the company.

Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):

When Tesla launched the base Model Y AWD in February, it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.

And the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.

Add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.

The timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.

Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.

If you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a new Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.

This is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk killed the Model S and Model X in January to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent new Tesla is the $61,990 Model Y L, which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.

We liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.

Now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.

There are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.

Great news. Can't wait for people to stop buying them and the company stops being a meme stock. It's about time EV shoppers recognized that there are indeed compelling options available.

And Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.

That’s a problem for a company whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.

How long before the $39,990 RWD goes the same way?

#4431. America's Top 3 SUVs Are About To Be Hybrid Or Electric

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Recent moves from Toyota and Honda prove it once and for all: Pure gasoline options just can't hang with electrified power anymore. On Thursday, Honda announced that its best-selling CR-V crossover will be available exclusively as a hybrid starting with a redesigned 2028 model.

"With a 100% hybrid powertrain, the next-generation Honda CR-V will further expand the appeal of America's most popular SUV as demand for hybrid-electric vehicles reaches record levels," said Luis Guerra, assistant vice president of Honda National Auto Sales.

Arriving next year, the 2028 CR-V will kick off a seventh generation for the SUV and be powered exclusively by a new two-motor hybrid system. Honda says the tech will boost driving efficiency and expand the range where the engine operates most efficiently, as compared with its current hybrid system. Today, the CR-V is available with both hybrid and pure-combustion powertrains.

Toyota made the RAV4 exclusively a hybrid starting with the 2026 model. Now Honda is following suit.

The Honda news follows similar decisions by Toyota, which made the RAV4 SUV hybrid-only starting with the 2026 model. (The Camry, too, is now only a hybrid.)

Taken together, it means that soon the top three models in the heart of the U.S. car market will come with some form of electrification. That alone will do a lot for getting people into more efficient cars—even if they aren't ready for an EV yet. In 2025, the RAV4, CR-V, and Tesla Model Y were America's best-selling SUVs, responsible for some 1.2 million sales combined.

The move should give a further boost to hybrid sales in America, which have already been on a tear. In the third quarter, hybrids reached 16% of the U.S. light-duty vehicle market. Chalk it up to growing awareness, higher gas prices, and more options in the marketplace.

Those options are poised to grow even further as more automakers capitalize on growing interest in hybrids—particularly in the SUV segment. Nissan is readying a Rogue Hybrid with a unique hybrid system that makes it drive a lot like an EV. GM is reportedly bringing hybrid powertrains to its three-row SUVs, like the Chevy Traverse and GMC Acadia.

In a sense, it's a wonder the hybrid boom didn't happen sooner. Getting a hybrid instead of a gas vehicle is essentially a no-brainer. You may pay a little more up front, but research shows that the fuel savings over time pay off the difference fairly quickly. According to Consumer Reports, the average hybrid commands a $1,700 premium, but most models pay for themselves within four years.

Just remember: Full EVs are still the cheapest vehicles to run per mile, if you have home charging. They'll always be better for the environment than hybrids too. And the smooth, quiet driving experience is tough to beat. More hybrid Hondas are a step in the right direction, but with the automaker bowing out of the EV game for now, buyers looking to ditch gas entirely will have to look elsewhere.

#4429. Arc Raiders patch nerfs the Deadline mine, ends the menace of the Venator

The first post-Stella Montis patch for Arc Raiders has arrived, and it predictably touches much of what people brought to the latest map.

Arc Raiders has received a new update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the new “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance issues with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark said pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

In today’s update, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

Another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

The patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

Beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

This change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

Check the official blog for the full change log for patch 1.3.0. If you’re just getting started with the hottest extraction shooter ever, our Arc Raiders tips offer plenty of help. #4428. Meta to deploy 25 electric semi trucks across I-10 corridor, but has nothing to ship

Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.

The second major trucking deal between Facebook parent company Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 new battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona. But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.

“Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, said Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”

Meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers’ alliance. The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May. This new Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.

This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The company adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy new trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”

Yuck. That's the feeling I get when reading this. Am I happy that more EV semi's will be going on the road? Yes. But the way it's being done just makes me feel dirty. And I refuse to do or have anything that Mark Zuckerberg is involved with. I find him to be disgusting. But then again I find most of these super wealthy people to be vomit inducing.

So I'd liken this deal to a guy who goes out to a bar with the sole intention of "having some fun". And it doesn't matter to him how that happens, as long as he gets his happy ending. But then when the sun rises and the darkness vanishes, who this guy slept with is revealed and it's not good.

Zucherberg isn't doing any of this for the planet. He's doing it for money.

Nevoya expects Meta’s fresh batch of semis to begin prowling I-10 in 2027, where they’ll cover approximately 4 million freight miles annually.

#4427. Slate Is Selling A $30 'Screenless GPS' For Its Low-Tech Truck

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Slate has introduced a new "Screenless GPS" for its bare-bones EV pickup. It has zero boot time, no subscription fees, unlimited battery life, and absolutely zero chance of telling you to make a left turn into an active construction site since it, well, doesn't actually do turn-by-turn directions.

If you haven't caught on yet, it's a book: Rand McNally's 2027 Road Atlas, to be precise. On Thursday, Slate added the map to its online store for $30, calling it "the original navigation system." Slate said it's available in limited quantities.

The new product is clearly tongue-in-cheek and a bit of a stunt, but it also speaks to what Slate is trying to pull off. The startup is betting that people are fed up enough with complicated, modern cars to embrace a no-frills EV with unpainted composite body panels, manual windows, and no big infotainment screen. That, of course, means no built-in navigation either.

Obviously, few drivers actually want to use a physical map these days. Fortunately, the Slate will come with a phone mount, so owners can continue using their favorite mapping apps, like Google or Apple Maps. And hey, maybe that Slate-branded Atlas could come in handy in a pinch.

"When it comes to tech, we believe you should use the devices and solutions you already know and love," Slate said Thursday. "Not because we don't like tech, but because we believe you already have everything you need to get where you're going."

That minimalist mentality is what has kept the battery-powered truck under $25,000. You get an LFP battery, a bed, some wheels, and freedom from the complexities of the modern automobile. And if you really do want to add on some extras, they can be as analog as a map, or as digital as your phone. Or as involved as an SUV kit with extra seats and a roof.

It's a bold bet in an era when cars seem to only be getting more expensive and more packed with screens. We won't have to wait too long to see if the gamble pays off. Slate plans to deliver its first trucks later this year.

#4426. Battlefield 6 may have actually done it: beaten Call of Duty

Battlefield 6 sales are setting all kinds of records, but one in particular has long eluded the Battlefield series.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

#4425. Here are the coolest e-motorcycles and gear we saw at EICMA 2026

Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase. That means that all of the newest electric motorcycle announcements happen in one place, and we get a chance to check out the coolest developments and most interesting new gear.

Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.

LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet, showing just how far the company has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.

The new S4 Honcho family was a major focus, including the street-oriented Honcho Street, off-road Honcho Trail, and newly unveiled Honcho Skate, a stripped-down addition to the modular platform. The booth also included LiveWire’s larger S2 electric motorcycles, creating a pretty broad spectrum from lightweight urban machines up through full-size highway-capable electric motorcycles.

The other big piece of the booth was DUST Moto, which LiveWire acquired earlier this year. The production-intent DUST Hightail was displayed alongside the newly revealed DUST Spur, giving LiveWire an immediate presence in the increasingly popular lightweight electric dirt bike category.

Add in STACYC’s electric balance bikes for young riders, and the entire booth almost looked like an electric two-wheeler progression chart: start a kid on a STACYC, move up through lightweight DUST and Honcho machines, and eventually graduate to a full-size LiveWire.

GR1T Motorcycles is a relatively young European electric motorcycle startup that caught my eye at EICMA with its G1 platform, a lightweight electric motorcycle designed and engineered in Italy. The basic recipe is pretty compelling: 130 km/h (81 mph) top speed, 11 kW of continuous power and 26.6 kW (36 hp) peak, all while weighing just 130 kg (287 lb).

Perhaps most importantly for urban riders, its roughly 6 kWh battery is actually split into two removable 3 kWh packs, meaning apartment dwellers can pull the batteries out and charge them inside. They’re big, but removing them is doable.

GR1T’s bikes therefore pack in around 50% more battery capacity than most electric motorcycles in this size and weight class, meaning roughly 50% more range, as well.

There are also some interesting and clever design choices, like the underslung rear suspension and the triple-camera system that includes front and rear dashcams plus a cockpit-facing camera for recording the rider.

The clever part of the overall design scheme is that GR1T isn’t developing a separate platform for every motorcycle. The same basic G1 chassis, motor, batteries, belt drive, and electronics underpin four versions: the G1S Street, G1X Scrambler, G1XR Raider, and utility-oriented G1M Mission.

Prices are set to start at €8,495 including VAT, putting these squarely in that emerging category of reasonably affordable, lightweight electric motorcycles that have enough speed for real-world commuting without chasing superbike performance.

There’s an important caveat, though: these aren’t production motorcycles yet. GR1T says it is currently fundraising, with factory development and pre-orders set to follow after funding closes and first deliveries now targeted for the first half of 2028.

So the bikes aren’t quite ready for primetime yet, but it’s definitely a company to watch.

Real Motors brought one of the more visually striking electric motorcycles to EICMA with Project: ARES, a futuristic electric café racer that the American startup describes as an “Electric Analog” machine – basically an attempt to preserve the raw, mechanical connection of motorcycling while ditching unnecessary screens and gadgetry.

And there’s plenty of performance underneath the sci-fi bodywork: Real Motors lists a 75 kW (100 hp) motor, a 15 kWh battery, a 120 mph (192 km/h) top speed, and an estimated weight of 485 lb (220 kg).

The analog analogy is spot on, with the display probably the simplest and most straightforward I’ve ever seen on an electric motorcycle. There’s also no app, no subscription, and no digital handcuffs. The bike is very much the electric equivalent of a simple ICE bike that just rides, albeit with a much nicer ride.

Unlike many of the futuristic concepts scattered around EICMA, ARES is actually headed toward limited production.

Real Motors plans to build just 250 examples in its first LOT 01 production run, with pricing starting at $20,000 and North American deliveries targeted for early 2027. European deliveries are expected after homologation is completed.

The company has also brought former LiveWire CTO Vance Strader onto the project as it makes the difficult transition from a very cool prototype into an actual production motorcycle.

I actually had the chance to do a spin on the bike, and so I’ll be reporting back on the experience. But you can tell from my smile below that the ride was quite an experience!

Seatylock has been my go-to e-bike lock company for several years now, and I use their locks for my several e-bikes and my wife’s e-bike too.

Now Seatylock has returned with some even more impressive locks. The company showed off its new Ultra D28 lock, which is both angle grinder-proof and wide enough to lock the wheel of a motorcycle. It solves the problem of how do you make a lock strong enough for a motorcycle but also small and light enough that you can actually carry it with you, unlike a massive chain lock that usually stays where you park your motorcycle overnight.

In the image below, you can see the shackle next to an exposed section demonstrating the diamond coating that essentially destroys angle grinder discs – even diamond coated discs.

The company also has a slightly smaller version of the same lock designed for bicycles.

Both will absolutely destroy even the toughest angle grinder discs. Sure, eventually someone could cut through them, but it may take a dozen discs and by that point the thief has moved on to an easier target.

At EICMA 2026, Royal Enfield continued expanding its electric motorcycle ambitions with its Flying Flea sub-brand, showcasing the scrambler-style motorcycle alongside its growing lineup of lightweight, retro-inspired electric motorcycles.

There were several interesting colorways and customized designs on display, showcasing the Flying Flea’s stylish design.

The new models blend Royal Enfield’s classic design heritage with modern electric technology, targeting urban riders and those looking for a fun, approachable electric motorcycle rather than a high-performance machine.

With distinctive styling, compact proportions, and an emphasis on accessible riding, the Flying Flea lineup represents Royal Enfield’s effort to carve out a place in the emerging market for smaller electric motorcycles while maintaining the character that has made its gasoline-powered bikes so popular.

Yamaha showed off its new NMAX E electric scooter, bringing battery-powered performance to one of the brand’s most recognizable urban scooter families.

Designed as an electric alternative to the popular gasoline-powered NMAX, the new model combines familiar sporty styling with a quiet, low-maintenance electric drivetrain aimed at everyday city commuting.

The NMAX E uses Yamaha’s new compact eAxle powertrain, shared with the larger-wheeled XENTER E, and delivers up to 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power, putting it in the 125cc-equivalent class.

With its practical step-through design, automatic operation, and approachable performance, the NMAX E represents another step in Yamaha’s push to electrify its urban mobility lineup, particularly in European markets where scooters are already a popular alternative to cars.

Segway showed off a new vision for safer electric scooters, including its futuristic X Cruiser concept that takes rider protection to a whole new level.

Rather than relying solely on traditional motorcycle safety equipment, the X Cruiser explores automotive-inspired features such as integrated seats with seatbelts, partial enclosures, and even a fully roofed version designed to offer additional protection from the elements.

The concept includes several configurations, ranging from a more conventional open scooter to a partially enclosed design and a fully covered model that looks like a cross between a motorcycle and a tiny electric car. While these designs are still concepts rather than production-ready scooters, they demonstrate how Segway is rethinking two-wheeled transportation by exploring ways to make electric scooters safer, more comfortable, and potentially more appealing to riders who might otherwise be hesitant to trade four wheels for two.

Eli Electric Vehicles took to EICMA 2026 to display its compact Eli Zero electric quadricycle, a tiny two-seat urban EV designed to offer much of the convenience of a car without the size, weight, or expense of a conventional automobile.

With its enclosed cabin, side-by-side seating, and ultra-compact footprint, the Eli Zero offers a practical alternative to larger vehicles for short city trips, combining the weather protection and comfort of a car with the maneuverability and efficiency of a much smaller vehicle.

The company revealed a more powerful L7e-class version of the Eli Zero that it had previously teased, expanding the vehicle’s capabilities beyond its existing L6e configuration. The new Race Edition also pushes the envelope farther with custom interior and a few extra accents to the body.

With growing interest in smaller, more efficient urban transportation, Eli’s presence at EICMA definitely underlined how the show is increasingly embracing electric mobility solutions that go beyond traditional motorcycles and scooters.

NIU showed off its latest lineup of electric scooters, continuing the brand’s push to make battery-powered two-wheelers a practical alternative to gasoline-powered urban transportation. Known for its sleek designs, connected technology, and approachable electric scooters, NIU highlighted models aimed at a range of riders, from everyday city commuters to those looking for more powerful machines capable of keeping up with faster urban traffic.

The company showed off several new models for the 2027 model year, with scooters that combine modern styling with features such as smartphone connectivity, smart security systems, and efficient electric drivetrains, all while maintaining the simplicity and low operating costs that make electric scooters so appealing.

While I didn’t see anything groundbreaking at the brand’s booth this year, the incremental updates look to push new tech features further throughout the brand’s many models, helping more of NIU’s offerings enter that premium level that the company has been known for.

For something a bit wilder, Honda shared its futuristic EV Outlier Concept, an electric motorcycle that explores what two-wheeled design could look like when engineers are freed from the constraints of traditional gasoline-powered motorcycles.

With its long, low-slung profile, radically different riding position, and futuristic bodywork, the EV Outlier looks more like something out of a science fiction movie than a conventional motorcycle. The concept features electric motors integrated into both wheels, giving it two-wheel drive while opening up new possibilities for packaging and weight distribution.

Rather than simply replacing a combustion engine with a battery and motor, Honda used the EV Outlier to rethink the entire motorcycle layout, demonstrating how electrification could lead to entirely new types of riding experiences.

While the bike remains a design concept with no announced production plans, it offers an intriguing glimpse into Honda’s vision for the future of electric motorcycles.

Vespa showed off its next-generation electric scooter lineup at EICMA, including electric versions of the Primavera, Sprint S, and Primavera Tech. While they don’t look radically different, there’s a lot more happening underneath the familiar steel bodywork.

A new Italian-made, rare-earth-free electric motor improves efficiency and performance, while the 45 km/h Primavera and Sprint S now feature removable batteries.

The faster 67 km/h Primavera Tech gets up to 90 km of WMTC range – a 12.5% improvement – along with an updated vehicle management system and more efficient charger.

#4424. 2027 Acura Integra Type S

See all results for new 2027 Acura Integra Type S for sale near 32712

The Acura Integra Type S is the swankier cousin of the boy-racer Honda Civic Type R. The two share their mechanical underpinnings and hatchback body style, but the Acura is dressed in a more respectable-looking outfit. A lusty 320-hp turbocharged inline-four is under the hood and mates exclusively to a six-speed manual transmission. The combination loves to spin its front tires excitedly, and it's a riot to drive.

An expertly tuned chassis gives the Integra Type S high-spirited handling, and it rides comfortably enough for long trips. The engineers responsible for this gem had driving enthusiasts in mind when this Acura was planned. The cabin is slightly upscale from the Civic Type-R as well, although not as much as you’d think given the six grand price delta between the two.

Expert Tip: Its premium badge and $ 56,000 price tag put the Integra Type S into contention with some European rivals that offer richer accommodations.

Compare the 2027 Acura Integra Type S with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.

Acura has added a limited-production Heritage Edition to the lineup for 2027. Only 700 will be offered in the U.S., all painted Blazing Phoenix Yellow and wearing special copper-colored aluminum wheels. The Heritage Edition is also emblazoned with black exterior badging and features a titanium shift knob.

The standard Integra Type S gets a few changes for the 2027 model year, too, including new gloss black wheels, yellow brake calipers, dark gray interior trim, and gloss black climate control knobs. Several features have been added as standard, such as memory settings for the driver’s seat and an exterior mirror tilt-down feature that can be set to automatically dip the mirrors when you shift into reverse.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

A 320-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four with 310 pound-feet of torque is the sole engine for the Integra Type S. Like the Civic Type R, the Integra Type S routes the power exclusively through a six-speed manual transmission and front-wheel drive with a limited-slip differential. Shifter action is wonderfully light and precise—this is one of the best manual shifters in the business—and clutch take-up is smooth and intuitive. With all 310 pound-feet of torque available at 2600 rpm, you could skip a shift or two without worry, but it'd be a shame to miss out on all the fun.

Objectively, roadholding and braking match the Civic Type R, with the Integra Type S pulling 1.02 g's on the skid pad and stopping from 70 mph in just 153 feet. Subjectively, the Civic feels ever so slightly more vivacious from behind the wheel. The Integra Type S knows how to chill in less demanding situations, slipping into an almost-calm cruising mode. All Type S models come with 19-inch wheels wearing summer tires, Brembo brakes, and an exhaust system with three center-mounted exhaust pipes.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

In Comparison: The Integra Type S's brisk 60-mph sprint time is nearly two seconds quicker than the 7.0-second time we posted with the standard six-speed Integra and just 0.2 seconds behind the last Civic Type R we tested.

The EPA estimates that the Integra Type S will deliver 21 mpg city, 28 mpg highway, and 24 mpg combined. It's also worth noting the Type S returned an impressive 31 mpg on our 75-mph highway fuel-economy test, three miles per gallon better than its EPA rating. For more information about the Integra Type S's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

In Comparison: The Audi S3 is slightly more efficient, earning EPA estimates of 23 mpg city and 31 mpg highway, as is the BMW M235 Gran Coupe with estimates of 24 mpg city and 33 mpg highway.

First Row: Acura plays the long game with the Type S's interior, favoring conservative design and quality materials over outright flash. There are plenty of parts shared with the Honda Civic under the skin, but Acura pulls styling elements from its SUVs to foster the familial vibe. Distinctive features include mildly bolstered sport seats upholstered with perforated, faux-suede fabric, “Type S” embossed headrests, and subtle touches including a Type S shift knob, boot, and steering wheel emblem.

Second Row: A pair of individual rear bucket seats and a small center console armrest replace the standard Integra's rear bench. There's room for two in back, but the lack of features such as rear air vents and seat heaters is a notable omission in a supposedly premium car.

Cargo Capacity: Thanks to its Civic roots, the Integra Type S offers the same 24 cubic feet of cargo room accessed via a large hatchback. We fit five carry-on suitcases in the trunk and managed to squeeze in a total of 18 with the rear seats folded.

The Type S gets the same 10.2-inch digital gauge cluster as the rest of the Integra lineup; a 9.0-inch infotainment touchscreen is standard. A wireless smartphone charging pad, a head-up display, and a pair of USB ports are also included. All versions come with a top-tier 16-speaker, 530-watt ELS Studio 3D premium audio system.

A host of driver-assistance features are included as standard in the Integra Type S, including automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control.

For information about the Integra Type S's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Acura offers a longer powertrain warranty than most of its competitors, with powertrain coverage stretching up to six years or 70,000 miles. Complimentary scheduled maintenance is also included, unlike the Audi S3 or the Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class.

#4423. Hyundai is overhauling the Kona, and it looks like it may still be offered as an EV after all

Hyundai is skipping the typical mid-cycle refresh and plans to launch a completely redesigned Kona, with a sleek new style and an updated high-tech interior.

It’s been nearly four years since Hyundai introduced the second-generation Kona, meaning, like most of its models, the compact SUV was expected to receive a mid-cycle refresh.

Hyundai is apparently going straight to the third-generation model instead. Earlier this year, early-stage prototypes were spotted in Korea that looked much boxier and more rugged than the current Kona.

Since then, several test mules have been captured testing in the US, Europe, and other regions, confirming the Kona will adopt a more upright, traditional SUV design similar to the new Santa Fe, Palisade, and Tucson.

#4422. PUBG's extraction shooter spin-off, Black Budget, is finally going to be playable next month

The most interesting development in the PUBG universe, PUBG: Black Budget, is almost ready to show itself off to a wider group of players.

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

The game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#4421. A Record Number Of Uber Miles Are Happening In EVs

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Uber’s electrification efforts are looking better with every quarter, and this year’s third quarter has shown that the giant ride-hailing company is serious about lowering its fleet’s emissions. That said, Uber is also aware that, based on current trends, its 2030 goals “continue to be out of reach.”

Let’s focus on the good news first. Last quarter, Uber drivers across the globe completed a whopping 207.4 million rides in EVs, which boils down to over 26 EV trips on the ride-hailing platform every second, on average. Compared to the same period last year, the number of EV trips on the platform is 52% higher, but the big stats don’t end here.

In Europe, one in five Uber trips were done in an EV, while one in ten Americans and Canadians who took an Uber in Q3 wound up in an electric car. On average, there were 434,000 EV drivers active on Uber from July through September globally, up 52% from the same period last year,

When looking at the charts provided by the ride-hailing company, the difference between Europe and the U.S. and Canada is astonishing. Even from the start of the chart, in Q1 2021, Europe had a consistent lead when it comes to electrification, but the two North American countries were left in the dust starting in the third quarter of 2024. European drivers flocked to EVs, helped by various incentives and a boost in the charging infrastructure, while Americans' and Canadians’ uptake stayed relatively flat. For its part, Uber has offered cash bonuses to drivers who wanted to switch to an EV.

Despite the upward trends seen in the charts provided by Uber, it’s not all good news. The company has missed almost all of its sustainability targets for 2025 and is well on its way to missing its goals for the end of 2030 by a wide margin.

Just as the number of EVs on the ride-hailing platform has increased, plenty of drivers chose gas- or diesel-powered cars to make an extra buck on Uber. In the U.S. and Canada, every mile that a passenger traveled on Uber resulted in an average generation of 318 grams of carbon dioxide. That’s better than 2024’s 340 grams, but worse than the 306-gram average in 2023.

A similar story can be found in Europe, though the average vehicle emissions caused by Uber trips are vastly smaller than in the U.S. and Canada. Last year, 186 g of CO2 were put into the atmosphere in Europe for every mile traveled by a passenger on Uber. The figure is lower than in 2024 and 2023, but higher than the 183 g average in 2022.

The company said that the large gap between Europe and the U.S. and Canada can be linked to two factors. First, European drivers prefer EVs and hybrids more than American and Canadian drivers, but the more stringent fuel economy reporting standards in the U.S. also contribute to this discrepancy.

In 2025, the ride-hailing giant had wanted to see 100% of rides in London and Amsterdam be zero-emission. The outcome was just 41%. Furthermore, 50% of all mobility miles in seven European capitals were envisioned as being completed in electric vehicles, but the year ended with just 32%.

By the end of the decade, 100% of rides in Canada, Europe, and the U.S. should be zero-emission, but Uber is realistic and knows that it’s highly unlikely that it will finish 2030 with these numbers. Still, the company says it’s “deeply committed to this transition,” even though many levers are outside of its control.

Broderdorf took medical leave from his position as Jeep’s CEO in August. He was replaced by Branden Coté, who retains his position as head of Jeep.

This isn’t Broderdorf’s first time at Dodge. He’s held seven different positions related to marketing, sales, product planning, and operations throughout his 25-year tenure at Stellantis. Dodge has been led by Matt McAlear since 2024, but McAlear has been spread thin at Stellantis since February, when he took over as Chrysler’s CEO and head of Alfa Romeo North America. The Moon-Prayer Night is the big in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The new update, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

The highly-anticipated Durin is at last the new playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

There’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. This is how you can earn the 4-Star Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, too.

#4418. Tesla stops selling every Cybertruck except the $109,990 Cyberbeast

Tesla is now only selling one version of the Cybertruck in the US: the tri-motor Cyberbeast, which just got another $7,500 price hike to $109,990.

The Dual Motor and Premium AWD trims are still listed on Tesla’s configurator, but both are greyed out and can’t be selected. So the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today costs $109,990, up 57% from $69,990 in early August.

Here’s what Tesla’s US configurator shows today with a Los Angeles delivery address:

A week ago, the Cyberbeast cost $102,490. Before that, it was $99,990. That’s a $10,000 (10%) increase in about a week on a truck that hasn’t changed: 320 miles of estimated range, 11,000 lbs of towing, and 0-60 mph in 2.6 seconds.

On November 6, the same day Elon Musk announced the end of Cybertruck production, Tesla raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. That made the $92,490 Premium AWD the entry point. Now it’s gone too, with no announcement. The configurator just stopped letting you pick it.

New inventory isn’t an alternative either. When we checked, Tesla’s inventory search showed no new Cybertrucks within 200 miles of Los Angeles.

This comes two days after Musk extended Cybertruck production through the end of summer 2027 to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” On Monday, he claimed the order rate “far exceeds” production and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.”

If there really is a backlog, cutting off the two cheaper trims is one way to cap it before the line shuts down. It also pushes whatever demand is left toward the most expensive, highest-margin version of the truck.

But the sales data doesn’t describe a truck with a demand problem in the other direction. We estimate Tesla delivered 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks in Q3, a pace of about 30,000 a year on a line with more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. And in February, Tesla was offering a dual-motor Cybertruck at $59,990 for “only the next 10 days.”

That’s $50,000 less than the cheapest Cybertruck you can order today. Nine months later.

Some of those $59,990 buyers are still waiting on delivery dates pushed into 2027. Tesla hasn’t said whether their orders, or any other Dual Motor and Premium orders in the queue, will be built before production ends.

Unlike the thousands of $59k CT orders that may never get manufactured I can guarantee that every high margin $110k CyberBeast order will be delivered before production ends.

This is the wind-down playbook, and it’s moving faster than I expected. Announce the end, raise prices, pull the cheaper trims, and sell the last trucks in their most expensive form. Tesla is squeezing as much as it can out of every remaining Cybertruck.

I don’t blame Tesla for wanting margin on a program it’s walking away from. But it makes the “order backlog” talk look like what we said it was: an end-of-life rush Tesla created by announcing the end, now being monetized with a $109,990 sticker. Not great for anyone who was told in 2019 that this truck would start at $39,900, or that the tri-motor version would cost $69,900.

If you want a Cybertruck that isn’t a Cyberbeast, you’re now shopping used. And I’d keep an eye on used prices, because a truck that’s going out of production with no cheaper new option could hold its value better than it has over the last two years.

#4417. Tesla Just Killed Its Cheapest All-Wheel-Drive Model Y

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Getting an all-wheel-drive Tesla Model Y just got a lot more expensive after the American company removed the entry-level version of the crossover from its online configurator.

The Model Y All-Wheel Drive, which used to cost roughly $42,000, is nowhere to be found on the automaker’s website, which means the most affordable dual-motor Model Y is now the Premium AWD trim that starts at $51,630.

Introduced in February, the now-defunct Model Y AWD came hot on the heels of the budget-oriented Model 3 Standard and Model Y Standard that debuted in October 2025 as more affordable, rear-wheel-drive-only versions of the company’s best-selling EVs. When the bare-bones Model Y AWD was introduced, Tesla also dropped the “Standard” badge from its lineup, though the other trims are still called “Premium” and “Performance”.

Powered by the same battery as the single-motor Model Y RWD, the discontinued Model Y AWD had the shortest claimed range in the Model Y lineup, with an EPA-estimated 294 miles on a full charge—54 miles less than the most affordable rear-driven crossover in Tesla’s lineup currently.

With two electric motors providing motivation, the dropped Model Y AWD could sprint from zero to 60 miles per hour in 4.6 seconds, 2.2 seconds faster than its single-motor counterpart, despite weighing roughly 200 pounds more.

The cheapest Model Y in Tesla’s lineup remains the basic RWD version, which starts at $41,630. Compared to the better-equipped and more expensive trims, the entry-level crossover comes with redesigned front and rear lights, passive shock absorbers, a lower 225-kilowatt maximum charging power, fewer speakers for the audio system, and seats trimmed in vegan leather and cloth. There’s no FM radio, no rear screen, no ventilated seats, and only the front seats are heated. Furthermore, while the glass roof is still installed, the base trim has a headliner that covers it entirely.

The discontinuation of the Tesla Model Y All-Wheel Drive is just the latest casualty in the company’s quest to slim down its passenger-vehicle lineup. Earlier this year, the Model S and Model X were axed, and their production line has been ripped out of the factory to make room for robots. More recently, Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced that the Cybertruck would be retired next year. Until that happens, the only trim remaining is the top Cyberbeast, which starts at $109,990.

There are no plans to replace the Model S and Model X, and the Cybercab two-seater will take over the Cybertruck’s floor space.

#4416. Battlefield 6 kicks off its first free trial post the Black Ops 7 launch to twist that knife

Activision has done its own fair share of Battlefield 6 counterprogramming prior to that game's release, and EA is here to repay the favour with Black Ops 7.

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

The recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was announced last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

#4415. 2028 Ford Mustang Cobra with a Race Car-Derived V-8 Is Worth Waiting For

The Cobra finally returns to the Mustang lineup and essentially resumes the track-focused role last held by the Shelby GT350.

Ford only just launched the Mustang Dark Horse SC earlier this year, but the Blue Oval brand isn’t letting up when it comes to high-performance versions of its iconic pony car. While the S650-generation Mustang introduced the new Dark Horse branding—at the expense of the legendary Shelby nameplate—and saw the arrival of the new $300,000-plus GTD, Ford’s upcoming Mustang variant revives a famous name from the past: Cobra. The new Mustang Cobra is expected to slot between the Dark Horse and Dark Horse SC as an indirect successor to the last Shelby GT350, providing track-ready performance and high-fidelity driver engagement.

The Shelby GT350, offered from 2015–2020, is considered one of the best Mustangs ever, thanks to its naturally aspirated flat-plane-crank 5.2-liter V-8 known as Voodoo. The last Cobra is also coveted by Mustang fans, so the new track-focused model has big shoes to fill. And with a new engine most likely under the Cobra’s hood, there’s potential for another legendary Mustang to be born.

The Cobra will continue to utilize the S650 platform, itself an evolution of the S550 chassis that underpinned the Mustang from 2015–2023. The Cobra will adapt the Mustang into a dedicated track car, and we think it will also spawn a more hardcore Cobra R with even more extreme aerodynamics, stronger brakes, and greater weight savings, potentially even removing the backseat. We expect the Cobra’s bodywork to be based on the Dark Horse SC, but with small tweaks and possibly a rear wing that harkens back to the 2000 Cobra R.

Mustang fans are obviously clamoring for the return of the Voodoo, but we don’t think that’s what Ford has in store. Fret not, however, because the automaker is cooking up something special for the new Cobra.

Instead of the 5.2-liter Voodoo, the new Cobra will pack a naturally aspirated 5.4-liter engine derived from the Mustang GT3 race car that has triumphed at the 24 Hours of Daytona and secured a podium at Le Mans. The Coyote-based GT3 engine features a cross-plane crank, but the teaser video released by Ford emitted a high-revving scream, so there’s a chance that the Cobra’s engine will switch to a flat-plane-crank setup. Still, if you’ve recently been to an IMSA race, you’ll know the GT3 car produces a thunderous soundtrack, so enthusiasts are in for an auditory treat regardless.

Although Ford hasn’t confirmed that the Cobra will adapt the GT3 race car’s engine, in the first teaser it said the car would pack a “heart born from racing.” We don’t expect the Cobra to come close to the Dark Horse SC or GTD in terms of power, but we wouldn’t be shocked if the 5.4-liter V-8 exceeds the 550 horsepower that the GT3 car is restricted to by racing regulations.

See all results for new 2028 Ford Mustang for sale near 12020

Better yet, the new 5.4-liter V-8 will be paired with a six-speed manual for maximum driver engagement. We think Ford will likely employ the Tremec TR-3160 transmission already used in the Dark Horse.

At the moment, the Mustang has the V-8 muscle car world all to itself. Dodge is expected to stuff a supercharged V-8 back into the Charger for the 2028 model year, while Chevy is gearing up to bring back the Camaro around 2028. The only other V-8-powered car under $100,000 is the Corvette, which has a completely different form factor with its mid-engine layout, but it will likely still be cross-shopped against the Cobra.

Pricing is probably the biggest risk. Ford needs to make sure it doesn’t alienate its customers by making it too expensive, given that the Dark Horse SC already has a hefty $105,585 asking price (about $20K more than the GT500 that it replaced). The new 5.4-liter V-8 will also have to make a strong impression as a successor to the much-loved Voodoo.

#4413. Audi A4 EV Delayed Amid VW Group Financial Troubles: Report

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Audi has delayed the introduction of the electric A4 sedan by roughly one year, according to Autocar, which quotes an inside source at the German automaker. The electric A4, which was supposed to go into production at the company’s main plant in Ingolstadt in 2028, will go head-to-head with the BMW i3 and Mercedes-Benz C-Class EVs, which are already available in Europe.

The delay is reportedly tied to the Volkswagen Group’s worsening financial situation, software woes linked to the long-delayed Scalable Systems Platform (SSP), and Audi’s desire to make significant changes to the underbody of what should have been a common design across SSP-based electric sedans.

The current-generation Audi A5, which replaced the A4, is available with a plug-in hybrid powertrain.

Autocar’s source said that the premium German automaker requested bespoke footwells for both front and rear passengers instead of the completely flat floor that many purpose-built EVs use today. The reason behind this big demand reportedly has to do with the brand’s desire to deliver the packaging, seating position, and interior proportions that have traditionally been offered by the A4.

What’s more, the BMW i3 rival will supposedly use a 48-volt electrical system for its accessories instead of the traditional 12V setup that had been planned originally. Just like in the Tesla Cybertruck, adopting a higher-voltage system enables the automaker to use thinner-gauge wire and install higher-powered computers.

However, the changes come at a tough time for Audi’s parent company, VW Group, which is ditching grandiose plans and doing everything it can to limit the cash bleeding. The upcoming Volkswagen ID. Golf, which is also based on the SSP architecture, has been delayed, leaving the marque with its current lineup of electric models until the end of the decade.

For what it’s worth, the VW Group’s new lineup of affordable EVs is doing very well in Europe, but the money problem persists. The company can’t make them fast enough to keep up with demand, but building gas cars is still more profitable. This conundrum has put the German auto industry giant in a tough spot, where it’s trying to keep factories alive, but the importance of the vehicles that are currently being assembled there is slowly fading.

The first SSP-based cars were originally planned for 2026, but so far, not a single production model has been assembled.

#4411. Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on the SSP

After delaying development of the long-awaited electric Golf, Volkswagen is delaying another EV based on its SSP platform.

As it scrambles to cut costs, Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer revealed in an internal memo at the end of October that development of the all-electric Golf is being delayed at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

The news comes after the VW Group posted an operating loss of €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the infamous Dieselgate scandal in 2015.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” Schäfer said in the memo reviewed by Reuters. The Wolfsburg plant, AKA the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.

Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer announced earlier this year that the long-awaited electric car was delayed until closer to 2030.

Schäfer suggested the delay was because the SSP (Scalable Systems Platform), which is being developed through its partnership with Rivian, was taking longer than expected, again due to costs.

According to Autocar, Volkswagen is now delaying the Audi A4 E-tron as well, another vehicle that was initially planned to be among the first based on the SSP platform.

Production of the electric A4 is being pushed back until at least 2029, a year later than originally planned. While the delay is disappointing for Audi fans (including myself) still waiting for an electric A4, it also puts Audi behind rival luxury brands in the mid-size sedan segment.

BMW has the new i3, and Mercedes-Benz has the C-Class EV, both of which feature major improvements in range, charging, and efficiency over their previous-generation EVs.

Volkswagen said in 2023 that the 800V SSP will serve as a “single future backbone with integrated electric and electronics architecture,” claiming that more than 40 million models were expected to be built on it.

The company also said investment and R&D costs were expected to be reduced by about 30% compared to the current MEB platform, enabling most models “to achieve the same margin compared to their conventionally powered counterparts.”

Volkswagen’s software struggles started in its internal division, Cariad, leading to delays, missed targets, and budget overruns.

To fix it, VW turned to Rivian, forming a joint venture to develop its next-gen software-defined vehicle (SDV) electrical architecture.

In March, VW said several test vehicles, including the ID.EVERY1, Audi, and Scout with the SDV architecture underwent “comprehensive evaluation,” and successfully validated over-the-air (OTA) functionality.

Being cash efficient is good, but delays to the next-gen platform that will keep you competitive with rival brands seem like a problem.

However, the Audi A4 E-tron delay is not entirely about software. The Autocar report claims Audi demanded significant changes to the SSP platform for the A4 E-tron so it more closely matched the current gas version.

Audi reportedly wanted individual footwells for front and rear passengers, which would require repositioning the battery.

The luxury brand also reportedly asked for a 48V electrical system instead of the traditional 12V setup initially planned.

While development of the Golf EV is on hold, VW’s works council said the pause will not delay its launch, promising to make up for lost time. It’s still expected to launch in 2030. The Audi A4 E-tron is now expected to arrive around 2029.

#4410. 2027 Aston Martin Valhalla

Aston Martin’s most outrageous road car is the Valhalla. This million-dollar miracle boasts a plug-in hybrid powertrain with 1064 horsepower and uses technology developed alongside Aston Martin’s F1 racing team. Its performance and handling are as incredible as you'd guess they would be.

You also might assume that the Valhalla is intimidating to drive, but in reality, it’s quite approachable. Other than having to get used to the absence of a rear window, the Valhalla is comfortable enough and easy enough to drive on the road that you conceivably use it as a daily driver—assuming you have the courage to commute in a car with a seven-figure price tag and the willingness to put up with the endless stares of passersby.

Expert Tip: The Valhalla’s dual-personality nature reminds us of another approachable supercar with over 1000 horsepower: the Corvette ZR1X, which costs a fraction of the Aston but offers similar performance and handling.

Compare the 2027 Aston Martin Valhalla with the top vehicles in this segment with our new compare tool.

There are no changes in store for the Valhalla for the 2027 model year, but an open-top Spider model is coming for 2028.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The Valhalla is motivated by a massively powerful plug-in hybrid powertrain. At its core is a Mercedes-AMG–sourced twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 with a flat-plane crank. It feeds the rear wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission and apportions torque via an electronically controlled limited-slip rear differential. Additionally, two electric motors power the front wheels and a third is integrated into the transmission. Combined output is 1064 horsepower.

Lightweight carbon fiber makes up the car's core structure. The Valhalla also features F1-style pushrod front suspension and employs a multi-link setup at the rear. Adaptive dampers and carbon-ceramic brakes are standard. Active aerodynamics are a major feature of the Valhalla, with movable front and rear wings that adjust to balance downforce and drag, maximize grip, and improve braking performance. When we drove the Valhalla, we found it to be remarkably engaging to drive for such a powerful, high-tech machine, more friendly on the road than you'd expect.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

In Comparison: When we test-drove the Valhalla, we estimated a 60-mph time of just 2.1 seconds. That would put Aston Martin’s supercar in the same league as other exotics, including the Ferrari 849 Testarossa, the McLaren 750S, and the Chevy Corvette ZR1.

The Valhalla’s electric-only range is a pitiful 5 miles per charge, but that’s enough for you to creep out of your neighborhood for a pre-dawn joyride without waking the neighbors. The battery's primary job is to feed the electric motors for the purposes of maximizing acceleration rather than driving range.

The EPA estimates that the Valhalla will deliver 13 mpg city, 19 mpg highway, and 15 mpg combined. If we ever get the chance, we’ll take the Valhalla on our 75-mph highway fuel economy route and then update this story with test results. For more information about the Valhalla’s fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

First Row: The Valhalla's interior deftly blends form and function. It features extensive use of carbon fiber, giving the cabin a unique visual character while keeping weight to a minimum. Sitting front and center before the driver is a rectangular F1-inspired steering wheel that features physical infotainment controls.

Forward of the steering wheel is a column-mounted digital display that shows a linear tachometer in Race mode and a speedometer and navigation information during road driving. A carbon brace runs the width of the cabin, on top of which floats a central infotainment screen that displays vital vehicle information, including battery charge level and energy-deployment data.

Cargo Capacity: Be sure to pack light or, really, not at all: the Valhalla does not have a trunk nor a luggage compartment of any kind.

The Valhalla's infotainment duties are handled by a centrally mounted 10.3-inch touchscreen. Aston Martin says that the Valhalla features bespoke infotainment software, but wireless Apple CarPlay comes standard.

The Valhalla offers a host of driver assists that are commonly seen on less extreme machines. While the Valhalla will feature conventional side mirrors, they'll be supplemented by a camera-based rearview display inside the cabin.

For information about the Valhalla's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Aston Martin provides limited and powertrain warranties that are on par with what other high-end automakers offer. However, unlike the competition, Aston doesn't include any maintenance visits in its coverage.

#4408. The VW ID. Buzz Is Getting A New Job As A Robotaxi

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The Volkswagen ID. Buzz hasn't exactly been a smash hit in the U.S. But that hasn't stopped commercial customers from eyeing up the nostalgic electric van for something it's particularly good at: moving people.

May Mobility announced on Thursday that it plans to integrate its autonomous driving systems into the Buzz to give it a job wherever driverless taxis are welcome.

May wants to use its existing tech stack to equip up to the ID. Buzzes with hardware and software that can see "up to 10 seconds into the future."

Well, kind of—May's tech uses onboard predictive modeling to anticipate how the world around it will move, similar how a human assess other drivers around them. It creates multiple scenarios in its digital brain and uses the model's reasoning to determine which one is most suited for its environment.

The tech would also make the cars capable of integrating with any of the "global robotaxi platforms," which is one of the ways that May is approaching its partnership-first business model. Presumably, that means its existing fleet partners like Lyft, Uber, and other ride hailing services around the world.

May's approach is also a silent win for folks who want to make sure that Buzz doesn't fizzle out.

One of the biggest blockers to Buzz adoption on the consumer side has been the price. While that could change in the coming months, the van's initially high price tag and just so-so range made it a fairly lukewarm offering to EV buyers looking to park the Buzz in their own driveway. That's why Robotaxis might be the best use of the Buzz yet.

It's roomy enough to comfortably haul plenty of passengers (and whatever cargo they bring along), plus it has the easy ingress and egress of a minivan. Other companies seem to agree, even VW's own MOIA arm that recently began testing an autonomous version of the Buzz in Los Angeles.

So far, May has completed about 600,000 commercial driverless rides in the U.S. and Japan. And while it hasn't said how many cars it operates, May is pretty open about its long-term goal for the Buzz.

It plans to put 10,000 of these autonomous ID. Buzzes on the road by 2031. That all starts with road testing early next year, followed by delivering the first fleet vehicles to customers by 2028.

The third-generation Tang joins the Great Tang, or Da Tang, as it’s called in China in BYD’s expanding flagship SUV lineup.

We knew it was coming soon after the new model appeared in a regulatory filing in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) last month.

BYD announced on Friday that pre-orders for the third-gen Tang are officially open, starting at 225,000 yuan, which is around $34,000.

The “large five-seat flagship SUV,” as BYD calls it, is available in three variants, priced from 225,000 yuan ($34,000), 240,000 yuan ($36,000), and 260,000 yuan ($39,000) with rear- and all-wheel-drive variants.

The two lower-priced variants are both RWD, offering a CLTC range of up to 850 km (528 miles), while the top-spec dual-motor AWD version has up to 770 km (478 miles).

All versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, enabling the battery to be charged from 10% to 80% in five minutes, or nine minutes to go from 10% to 97%.

Inside, the five-seat SUV packs a surprising amount of tech and premium extras for the price. The setup features two massive screens: a 35.4″ integrated display and another 30″ panoramic theater screen.

Unlike its predessor, which offered five and six-seat configurations, the third-gen Tang will only be offered as a five-seater.

The five-seat setup opens up interior space for passengers and the third-gen Tang has the largest front trunk (frunk) in its class at 205L, BYD said.

Like many of its new flagship vehicles, the third-gen Tang is equipped with BYD’s latest tech, including its God’s Eye B driver-assistance system and Disus-A dual-chamber intelligent air suspension body control system.

Other added features include a 22-speaker Dynaudio sound system, intelligent electric all‑wheel drive, a high-speed tire blowout stability system, and its iTAC intelligent torque control system.

Lu Tian, the general manager of BYD’s Dynasty division said third-gen Tang vehicles have arrived at dealerships nationwide.

Why mention "two enormous screens" like they are some markers of a more premium vehicle or represent some value? We don't measure the utility of cars by screen real estate per dollar. It's the other part of the utility that matter: range, driving dynamics, road trip convenience, fit/finish/materials/insulation. Personally, I don't think "enormous screens" are going to age well as an automotive trend.

The Great Tang received over 150,000 preorders by the time it launched in mid-June, a record for a single BYD model.

Since its official launch, the larger Great Tang (Da Tang) has sold more than 10,000 units for four straight months now.

The Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500) a CLTC driving range of 800 km (497 miles). Starting at just 269,900 yuan ($40,000), the Flagship EV version uses a bigger (130.15 kWh) battery, offering a CLTC range of up to 590 miles (950 km).

Will BYD’s smaller five-seat SUV draw the same demand? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.
